title: Make registered contracts refuse in production, not only when an agent remembers to validate

AC1.note: src/gdskills/contracts.ts carries a required discriminated ContractEnforcement per contract — machine-readable, not prose. Every kind:production entry names a real non-test module, and the guard opens that module and requires the actual loadSchema("<name>") call: a claim naming a file that does not load the schema fails. Proved by pointing the claim at src/lib/templates.ts, which the guard rejected by name.

AC2.note: keryx review comments reply --result <file> validates against review-pr-feedback-output before the pass is built and before any network call. Demonstrated by running the real CLI from source in review-result-contract.test.ts: the AC2 payload (mode analyze with a populated fix) exits non-zero with '$.fix: Expected type null, got object', and the success header never prints. Required expressing the rule as a conditional first — it lived in the fix property's DESCRIPTION, the same defect this skill's input contract had. Mutation-proved: removing the gate call fails the tests.

AC3.note: All seven unenforced contracts carry kind:none plus a written reason, and the guard rejects an empty one. The reasons distinguish 'no keryx process is on this path' (agent-to-agent payloads) from 'keryx does not read this file back' (task-implementer-output vs subagent-result), so the reader can tell the two apart.

AC4.note: contract-enforcement.test.ts derives the split from CONTRACTS and checks the discriminant at runtime as well as in the type, because a cast can land in neither group while the compiler is satisfied. Verified with in-memory fake registrations: no enforcement declared, a production claim naming a non-loading file, a claim naming a file that does not exist, a test file as the enforcement point, and an empty reason — five negatives, each failing with its own message. Plus an anti-vacuity test pinning that both groups are non-empty and the registry has at least 11 entries.

AC5.note: Swept the three phrasings the AC names. 'refuses a malformed one. Validate before dispatching' in review-pr-feedback's SKILL.md is ACCURATE and left alone: it says the validate COMMAND refuses, then instructs the agent to run it, which matches the recorded kind:none. 'is BLOCKED' matched only gdctx transcripts. Two unbacked claims were found outside the listed phrasings and corrected: harness/child/contract.ts and harness/extension/execute.ts said the extension metadata 'validates against' harness-child-contract-extension.schema.json, which nothing loads — now stated as SHAPED by the TypeScript types.

AC6.note: Full suite 8416 pass, 18 skip, 0 fail. tsc --noEmit 0 errors. bun run lint clean. keryx skills verify --bundled clean — run FROM SOURCE, because the installed 0.2.86 reported parity while the working tree's schema copy was stale; both generated copies resynced. One rejecting payload per enforced contract pinned in contract-enforcement-regression.test.ts, with a conforming value asserted to pass so the rejections are not a validator broken shut.
